the following question: How can we learn an effective policy without evaluating actions outside of the data?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we propose a new offline reinforcement learning method that never needs the value of unseen action during training, but still enables learned policy to improve over the behavior policy.
IQL can learn a policy that substantially improves over the behavior in the dataset, without ever querying unseen actions, and with only a small additional cost in computation.
IQL can learn a policy that is much better than behavior policy in the dataset without ever querying out-of-sample action.
The main takeaway from our work is that

offline RL can be made more sample-efficient by leveraging the generalization capacity to implicitly approximate the value of the policy improvement step, without ever explicitly querying out-of-sample Q-values.
offline RL does not need to explicitly query unseen actions during training, and instead can implicitly generalize by treating the value function as a randomized variable.
the value of the optimal action can be approximated implicitly by treating the value as a random variable and then estimating its upper expectile.
